**Proof.**

Let \(k\) be a real closed field. By the Artin–Schreier theorem, \(k\) admits a unique field ordering, and under this ordering an element \(a\in k^{*}\) is a square if and only if \(a>0\).

Since \(-1<0\) in any ordered field, \(-1\notin k^{*2}\). Now take any \(a\in k^{*}\).

- If \(a>0\), then \(a\in k^{*2}\), so \([a]=[1]\) in \(k^{*}/k^{*2}\).
- If \(a<0\), then \(-a>0\), so \(-a\in k^{*2}\), and \(a=(-1)(-a)\in (-1)\cdot k^{*2}\), giving \([a]=[-1]\).

Hence
\[
k^{*}=k^{*2}\;\sqcup\;(-1)\cdot k^{*2},
\]
a disjoint union, so the square class group \(k^{*}/k^{*2}\) has exactly two elements: \([1]\) and \([-1]\). It is cyclic of order \(2\), generated by \([-1]\), and therefore
\[
k^{*}/k^{*2}\cong \mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}\cong \mu_{2}.
\]

### PROOF COMPLETE
